label: Sütlaç
note: Turkish rice pudding, often baked (fırın sütlaç) until the top browns; name from sütlü aş, dish with milk; may be sweetened with sugar or pekmez; eaten by Sephardic Jews at Shavuot

about.text: Turkish rice pudding of milk, rice and sugar, often baked in clay dishes.

sources.text: The first paragraph of its article, shortened.
The photograph, its author and its licence, from its page.

how.text: Cooked sütlaç is poured into bowls and baked only to brown the skin, which is what makes the fırın version. Amounts are for 6 servings from yemek.com; the Hamsiköy version cooks rice in boiled milk with butter for about 15 min before the sugar goes in.

sources.text: The table, the facts and the words on how it is made, from these.

steps.name: boil
steps.note: Rice, 1/2 tea glass, boiled first in 1.5 cups water.
1 l of milk is added with the sugar and cooked.

steps.name: thicken
steps.note: 1.5 tbsp cornstarch whisked with lukewarm water and 1 egg yolk.
Boiled a couple of times, then vanilla is added.
In a water bath until the tops brown.

facts.v: Old Ottoman recipe: rice boiled in water, strained, cooked soft in milk, sugar added at the end (Melceü't-Tabbâhîn)
